user.title: Add a Harman EasyTouch stove
user.description: Pick the power sensor (watts) for this stove. It is only used to build the 20 second moving average. Choose an existing profile, or choose "Import / design a new profile" to continue to the profile editor.

data_description.name: A name for this stove, for example "Living room stove".
data_description.source_entity: A sensor that reports the stove's electrical power draw in watts, for example from a smart plug or energy monitor. It is only used to build the 20 second moving average.
data_description.profile: The thresholds and timings used to work out the stove's state. Pick a profile, or choose "Import / design a new profile…" to open the JSON editor.

import_profile.title: Import / design a profile
import_profile.description:
Paste profile JSON, or edit the example below. The profile is saved under its "name" and used for this stove. Built-in profile names cannot be overwritten.

Thresholds and timings both refer to the `moving_average` attribute, and all five timing keys are optional.

**Thresholds**

Each value is the lower limit of a state, in watts. A state applies when the sensor's `moving_average` is above that state's threshold and not above the next state's threshold up. Values must strictly decrease from `ignite` down to `idle`. At or below the `idle` value the state is `sensor_fault`.

**Timings**

A state change only becomes final after the new state has held for a set number of seconds. Each state's timings apply when moving into that state. The states have a fixed order: `sensor_fault`, `idle`, `extinguish`, `post_ignite`, `fault_extinguish`, `cool_down`, `burn_1` to `burn_6`, `ignite`. All keys are optional.

| Key | Seconds to wait when... | If missing |
|---|---|---|
| `sequp` | moving up one step into this state | 0 |
| `seqdown` | moving down one step into this state | 0 |
| `nonseq` | jumping more than one step (for example `burn_1` to `burn_3`) | 0 |
| `cascadeup` | moving up one step after an unfinished change | uses `sequp` |
| `cascadedown` | moving down one step after an unfinished change | uses `seqdown` |

A change is "unfinished" when the state changes again before the previous change became final. Example: the stove is at `burn_1` and moves to `burn_2`, but before the wait ends it moves to `burn_3`. The wait for `burn_3` then uses `cascadeup` instead of `sequp`. A new change always cancels the one still waiting.

init.title: Harman EasyTouch options
init.description: Change the power sensor or profile for this stove, and how long to keep the last state when the sensor drops out. To edit the profile JSON, tick "Edit profile JSON" and select Submit.

data.unavailable_delay: Keep last state when the sensor drops out (seconds)

data_description.source_entity: A sensor that reports the stove's electrical power draw in watts, for example from a smart plug or energy monitor. It is only used to build the 20 second moving average.
data_description.profile: The thresholds and timings used to work out the stove's state.
data_description.unavailable_delay: How long to keep showing the last state after the power sensor becomes unavailable, including while it starts up after a Home Assistant restart. Set to 0 to show the stove as unavailable immediately.
data_description.edit_profile: Tick this and select Submit to open the JSON editor for the selected profile. Built-in profiles are saved as a copy under a new name.
